# ui::testing::HeadlessWindowHost

Header: `winui/testing/HeadlessUI.hpp`.

The in-memory window host [HeadlessUI](headless-ui.md) installs. It follows the same window-state rules as the real host without a native window, so window-state and title-bar tests can drive it.

- Requests apply synchronously by default. Set [`defer_requests`](#defer_requests) to queue them instead, so a test can observe the gap between a request and the system's answer, then call [apply_pending_requests()](#apply_pending_requests) to let them land.
- [simulate_state()](#simulate_state) is the other direction: the user clicking the caption's maximize button, or Win+Down. It reports the new state without anyone having asked.
- Everything the window sends the host is recorded, and [click_system_menu_item()](#click_system_menu_item) and [click_thumbnail_button()](#click_thumbnail_button) stand in for the user picking an entry.

Like the real host, it remembers the normal bounds across minimize and maximize, and whether full screen was entered from maximized, so [restore()](#restore) goes back to the right place.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::testing::HeadlessUI ui;
ui::Window& window = ui.window();

ui.host().defer_requests = true;
window.request_state(ui::WindowState::Maximized);
REQUIRE(window.state().get() == ui::WindowState::Normal); // asked, not yet answered
ui.host().apply_pending_requests();
REQUIRE(window.state().get() == ui::WindowState::Maximized);

window.set_system_menu({{.text = "Always on top", .on_click = [&] { /* ... */ }}});
REQUIRE(ui.host().click_system_menu_item(0));

window.close();
REQUIRE(ui.host().close_requests == 1);
```

## defer_requests

```cpp
bool defer_requests = false
```

When true, requests are queued instead of applied (see the class comment).

## normal_bounds

```cpp
Rect normal_bounds {0.0f, 0.0f, 800.0f, 600.0f}
```

The bounds a restore to Normal lands on, and what [bounds()](#bounds) reports.

## frame

```cpp
Thickness frame {}
```

What the frame takes around the client area, for [resize()](#resize) and the size limits.

## screen_work_area

```cpp
Rect screen_work_area {0.0f, 0.0f, 1920.0f, 1040.0f}
```

What [work_area()](#work_area) reports.

## close_requests

```cpp
int close_requests = 0
```

How many times [close()](#close) was called.

## style_applications

```cpp
int style_applications = 0
```

How many times [set_style()](#set_style) was called.

## activations

```cpp
int activations = 0
```

How many times [activate()](#activate) ran.

## wake_requests

```cpp
std::atomic<int> wake_requests {0}
```

How many times [wake()](#wake) was called; atomic since [wake()](#wake) may come from any thread.

## HeadlessWindowHost

```cpp
HeadlessWindowHost(Window& window)
```

A host for `window`, which must outlive it. Does not install itself; [HeadlessUI](headless-ui.md) does.

## ~HeadlessWindowHost

```cpp
~HeadlessWindowHost()
```

## HeadlessWindowHost

```cpp
HeadlessWindowHost(const HeadlessWindowHost&) = delete
```

## operator=

```cpp
HeadlessWindowHost& operator=(const HeadlessWindowHost&) = delete
```

## request_state

```cpp
void request_state(WindowState state)
```

Applies `state` at once and reports it back, or queues it while [`defer_requests`](#defer_requests) is set.

## restore

```cpp
void restore()
```

Leaves Minimized/Maximized/Fullscreen for the state it came from; queued like [request_state()](#request_state) while [`defer_requests`](#defer_requests) is set.

## close

```cpp
void close()
```

Only counts the request in [`close_requests`](#close_requests); the window is not destroyed.

## wake

```cpp
void wake()
```

Only counts the request in [`wake_requests`](#wake_requests); safe from any thread.
